payload.claim: The spec declares `risk: standard`, but its `touches` list includes `saffron/cell/session.py`, which matches `saffron/cell/**` in `.saffron/policy.yaml`'s `elevate_on` list (the same list DESIGN.md's "Risk tiering" paragraph names explicitly). Per `policy.effective_risk`, the cell's actual risk tier at run time will be computed as `elevated` regardless of the frontmatter's `standard`, making the `size` gate blocking rather than advisory for this run. This has no effect on outcome since the prototype's measured total (212 + 889 = 1101 changed tokens) sits well under the `bug` ceiling of 1300 either way, and the system already reports the effective tier correctly in the PR body independent of what the spec declares, so there is nothing for the operator to fix before the cell starts.
